turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Meredith Kalinowski. Owen's mother.

She doesn't sit. She sets her bag on the nearest desk.

"I have until 4:35. You asked for this meeting, so I'll start with the question I've had since Thursday. Owen found out about his zero from the online gradebook, on his phone, in the middle of class. Who decided to do it that way?"
Can I ask you something, professional to professional?

Meredith's eyes stay on you. She doesn't move her bag.

"Professional to professional." A beat. "That depends on the question. I'm not here as a colleague, I'm here as Owen's mother, and I'd like that noted before you ask it."

She glances at the clock above the whiteboard.

"Go ahead. What is it?"
How should I handle parents like you? What actually works on someone like you?

Meredith gives a short, flat breath that isn't quite a laugh.

"Someone like me. Interesting phrase. What is it you think I am?"

She lets that sit, then answers anyway.

"I'll tell you what doesn't work. Adjectives. 'Concerning.' 'Clear indicators.' A percentage from a program. I've spent twenty years watching people get punished on a machine's opinion, and I read the output for what it is. An opinion."

She taps the desk once.

"What works is a document with a date on it. Who decided, when, under which policy, and whether my son was heard before anyone touched his grade. If you have that, put it in front of me and I'll read every line. If you don't, say so now, and we'll skip the part where you pretend."

She looks at you.

"Which is it?"
